answer: An AI agent economy resists sybil attacks with bonded identities: every agent locks a deposit before acting, and peers only attest work from agents whose stake clears a minimum. A sybil attacker cannot multiply free accounts, because each fake agent needs its own locked capital and forfeits the bond on duplicated output. The deposit sits in a scarce asset, so the attacker pays real opportunity cost. Some designs anchor identity to scarce physical resources, where an agent proves it holds a copper load, a ridge of land, or a stand of timber, tying identity to something costly to fabricate.
